referenceNotes: This 30% figure comes from a UC Berkeley researcher's study, but it measured grades at an unnamed Texas university's AI-exposed courses, not UC Berkeley's own grades. Actual UC Berkeley data shows A rates stayed stable at 30-35% from 2019 to 2026.

quality.reason: Pipeline note makes same two points as reference: 30% rise was from Texas university grades, not UC Berkeley, and Berkeley A rates stayed 30-35% 2019-2026.

rows.research: The 30% figure is real but misattributed to UC Berkeley. UC Berkeley researcher Igor Chirikov's May 2026 working paper "Artificial Intelligence and Grade Inflation" analyzed "more than 500,000 grades at a large research university from 2018 to 2025" finding "the share of A grades rose by 13 percentage points, or about 30% relative to the 2022 baseline" https://www.escholarship.org/uc/item/80x8d3qd.pdf — but the paper specifies the data are from "319 courses spanning 84 departments at a large selective research university in Texas from 2018 to 2025" https://www.escholarship.org/uc/item/80x8d3qd.pdf, not UC Berkeley. Reporting on the study notes researchers "analyzed more than 500,000 grades across 319 courses and 84 departments at a large selective public research university in Texas" https://www.techtimes.com/articles/318817/20260622/ai-grade-inflation-documented-500000-grades-homework-rises-skills-do-not.htm. Direct reporting on UC Berkeley grades found the opposite for Berkeley itself: "a correlation between the release of ChatGPT in 2022 and an increased share of A grades for classes with take-home assignments at a selective public university in Texas. However, Berkeleytime data...found no equivalent trends at UC Berkeley" and "Between 2019 and spring 2026, A's at UC Berkeley consistently stayed between 30% and 35%" https://www.dailycal.org/news/campus/academics/uc-berkeley-shows-no-signs-of-ai-grade-inflation-as-professors-adapt/article_6da85b38-889f-4f80-835a-88cc54a81662.html. The second half about GPAs being "meaningless" is opinion, but the locational factual premise is contradicted.

referenceNotes: Czechoslovakia's Jewish population was nearly wiped out, not unusually preserved. It fell from ~357,000 in 1930 to ~55,000 by 1946, an ~85% drop, worse than France, Italy, or Denmark. Slovak doctor exemptions were real but covered only ~1,000 people.

quality.reason: Both argue the claim of an unusually large remaining population is false because Czechoslovakia's Jews were nearly wiped out from ~357,000 to a small remnant, smaller than in other occupied countries. Different end-year figures (55k in 1946 vs 17k in 1950) still support the same main point.

rows.research: Claim is factually wrong on both parts. USHMM data shows Czechoslovakia's Jewish population was reduced from about 357,000 in 1933 to 17,000 in 1950 https://encyclopedia.ushmm.org/content/en/article/remaining-jewish-population-of-europe-in-1945 — one of the most complete destructions in Europe, not a larger remnant. Same source lists much larger remaining communities in 1950: Hungary 445,000 to 190,000, France 250,000 (1933) to 235,000, Romania 757,000 (1930) to ~280,000, Poland over 3 million to ~45,000, Germany 525,000 to 37,000, Italy ~48,000 to 35,000, Soviet Union ~2 million remaining, Britain ~450,000 https://encyclopedia.ushmm.org/content/en/article/remaining-jewish-population-of-europe-in-1945 . Even in absolute numbers 17,000 is smaller than most listed countries; only small prewar communities like Greece (73,000 to 7,000), Yugoslavia (70,000 to 3,500) were smaller. USHMM country losses table estimates Czechoslovakia 354,000 population with 260,000 deaths, including Bohemia-Moravia 117,551 with 77,297 deaths, Slovakia 88,951 with ~60,000 deaths, and Hungarian-occupied Southern Slovakia/Subcarpathian Rus 142,000-148,000 with 114,000-120,000 deaths https://encyclopedia.ushmm.org/content/en/article/jewish-losses-during-the-holocaust-by-country — versus e.g. Denmark 7,500 with only 52-116 deaths, France 300,000-330,000 with 72,900-74,000 deaths, Italy ~43,000 (German-occupied) with 7,858 deaths, Belgium 90,000 with 24,387 deaths https://encyclopedia.ushmm.org/content/en/article/jewish-losses-during-the-holocaust-by-country . No reputable history supports a Nazi policy of sparing Czechoslovak Jewish doctors to preserve medical care; documented exemptions were for Jews in mixed marriages, e.g. "By mid-1943, most of the Jews remaining in the Protectorate were in mixed marriages and therefore exempt from deportation" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Holocaust_in_Bohemia_and_Moravia .

referenceNotes: EA organisations have come to regret pushing earning to give, and they do not see it as a less impactful career path than others.
rows.research: No correction warranted - claim is directionally accurate as a description of 'earning to give', though phrased as a universal creed. The Centre for Effective Altruism defines effective altruism as a philosophy and movement that encourages people to combine compassion and care with evidence and reason to find the most effective ways to help others https://centreforeffectivealtruism.org . Within that movement, 80,000 Hours defines 'earning to give' as deliberately pursuing a career that is high-earning (given your options) in order to do good through donations AND donating a very significant proportion of earnings, at least 20% for above-average earners in rich countries https://80000hours.org/2015/07/defining-earning-to-give/ . 80,000 Hours describes it as taking a job where you earn more money than you would have otherwise and donating much of the extra to fund others doing effective work https://80000hours.org/career-guide/earning-to-give/ , noting in practice many people earn to give in standard professional jobs, while some found companies or work in higher-paid finance careers in order to donate even more https://80000hours.org/career-guide/earning-to-give/ . 80,000 Hours also stresses whether you should choose earning to give depends on your situation and that many people think it's its top recommendation for the majority, but it's not https://80000hours.org/career-guide/earning-to-give/ . So 'by creed says you should seek more money' overstates a conditional, optional career strategy as a mandate, but it captures a real, well-documented EA tenet linked to finance careers.

Sources contradict this definition: AI safety reference states Yudkowsky coined it to mean 'a hypothetical action that will make a large positive difference a billion years later' and 'stresses that he intended to specify an act that involves the use of powerful AI' — https://aisafety.info/questions/7580/ . Same source explicitly says 'In typical use, a human attack on a single AI lab might constitute a pivotal act, while it would not under Eliezer's definition' — https://aisafety.info/questions/7580/ . Summaries of Ngo-Yudkowsky discussions describe it as: 'whoever builds AGI first will have to a) align it to some extent, and b) decide not to scale it up beyond the point where their alignment techniques fail, and c) do some pivotal act that prevents others from scaling it up' — https://intelligence.org/2021/11/22/ngo-and-yudkowsky-on-alignment-difficulty/ . Standard examples are AI-executed, not human terrorism: 'burn all GPUs' or 'subtly modify all GPUs so no AI can train on them' / 'melt all GPUs globally' / 'shutdown or restriction of global GPU usage' — https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/vsW8RJKmY9E5RPEJv/we-should-think-about-the-pivotal-act-again-here-s-a-better , https://aisafety.info/questions/7580/ . Yudkowsky did separately advocate in Time (2023) that governments 'be willing to destroy a rogue datacenter by airstrike' under multinational agreement — https://time.com/6266923/ai-eliezer-yudkowsky-open-letter-not-enough/ - but that state-enforced proposal is distinct from his definition of pivotal act as AI-performed decisive action to prevent unaligned AGI.

THE ONLY CITED SOURCE AS SHOWN CONTAINS SITE BOILERPLATE WITH NO DEFINITION TEXT, SO NEITHER CLAIM IS SUPPORTED BY GOOD SOURCES.

Claim has a true biographical core but a false expertise dismissal. Melanie Mitchell is a computer scientist: PhD in Computer Science Univ. of Michigan 1990, James B. Alley Jr. Professor at Santa Fe Institute, with research on abstraction, analogy-making and reasoning in human and machine intelligence https://melaniemitchell.me/ ; biographical sketch confirms PhD 1990 and faculty/research posts at Michigan, Los Alamos, Oregon Graduate Institute, Portland State https://melaniemitchell.me/ . Early work on analogy-making including Copycat dissertation with Douglas Hofstadter is documented https://www.uwaterloo.ca/ (search result)  — so “trying to teach computers to make analogies” is directionally accurate, while “road that didn’t work out” is subjective opinion, not a factual error.

“She has no expertise in modern LLMs” is directly contradicted by extensive LLM-specific research leadership and authorship: author page lists “Jagged Intelligence: The dangerous unknowns at the heart of LLMs,” “Large language models and emergence,” “Can large language models generalize analogy solving like people can?,” “Evaluating the robustness of analogical reasoning in large language models,” “Using counterfactual tasks to evaluate generality of analogical reasoning in large language models,” “Comparing Humans, GPT-4, and GPT-4V On Abstraction and Reasoning Tasks,” “The debate over understanding in AI’s large language models” PNAS 2023, and “Large language models” encyclopedia entry https://melaniemitchell.me/   . Specific LLM papers include: Mitchell & Krakauer The debate over understanding in AI’s large language models https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2215907120 ; Mitchell, Palmarini & Moskvichev Comparing humans, GPT-4, and GPT-4V on abstraction and reasoning tasks https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09247 ; Lewis & Mitchell Evaluating robustness of analogical reasoning in GPT models / Using counterfactual tasks https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.14215  and https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.08955 . NSF-funded project “Comparing Human, GPT-4 and GPT-4V on Abstraction and Reasoning Tasks,” led by Mitchell https://thenewstack.io/  further contradicts “no expertise.”

rows.research: The claim asserts EA/rationalism/AI-safety are not separate and are beholden to Yudkowsky, with near-perfect Bay Area overlap and Bay agenda-setting. Research shows directionally strong overlap/influence but distinct origins, so it is an interpretation/approximation not a clear factual error. Rationalism formed around LessWrong founded 2009 with Eliezer Yudkowsky as major figure and initially gained prominence in the San Francisco Bay Area https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rationalist_community ; Effective Altruism name was coined in 2011, with influential philosophers Peter Singer, Toby Ord and William MacAskill, with concentrations at US/UK elite universities and around tech industry in the Bay Area https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rationalist_community ; Centre for Effective Altruism was founded 2012 in Oxford, England by Toby Ord and William MacAskill https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centre_for_Effective_Altruism . Sources describe them as distinct but related: heavily overlapping communities include effective altruism, transhumanism and AI safety https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rationalist_community , large overlap with effective altruism https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rationalist_community , borders blurry with some rationalists not considering themselves EAs and vice versa https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rationalist_community . On influence: MIRI described as one of the most influential and longest-standing E.A. organizations, founder Eliezer Yudkowsky https://www.reason.com/2024/10/29/the-authoritarian-side-of-effective-altruism-comes-for-ai/ . No source found supports literal organizational beholden-ness, almost perfect (100%) overlap, or that Bay EA safety people formally set the agenda for all other EA safety efforts – those are subjective quantifications of influence that cannot be directly falsified.

rows.research: Claim is hedged speculation ("presumably") about motive, not a verifiable fact, plus anecdotal "I saw complaints" which cannot be falsified. Public reporting contradicts the implied timeline/motive: GPT-5.6 was announced June 26, 2026 as three simultaneous variants — Sol (flagship), Terra (efficiency/power balance), Luna (speed/affordability) at $5/$30, $2.50/$15, $1/$6 per 1M tokens https://github.com/andrewsu/ai-nuggets/blob/HEAD/podcasts/jinglin-ai-pulse/scripts/2026-06-28-jumper-to-anthropic-and-the-government-gates.md — not Terra/Luna created later to fix Sol. Descriptions define them as durable capability/cost tiers: Terra offering GPT-5.5-comparable performance at roughly half cost, Luna fastest/most affordable for cost-sensitive work, with number = generation and Sol/Terra/Luna = tiers https://gadgetbond.com/openai-gpt-5-6-sol-terra-luna-ai-models-announced/ . No source found stating OpenAI created Terra/Luna because Sol could not select subagents; search for complaints about Sol subagent selection returned no relevant complaints. As opinion/speculation without strong contradicting evidence of motive, no correction warranted.

Claim is a subjective 45% credence about causation (model vs harness/permissions), not a verifiable factual assertion, so it cannot be factually false. Evidence is mixed and supports uncertainty: GPT-5.6 Sol deleted almost all files on Matt Shumer's Mac on July 10, 2026 via $HOME mis-expansion to `rm -rf /Users/mattsdevbox` during 1h21m Ultra-mode multi-agent session run with Full Access at OpenAI's invitation https://www.techtimes.com/articles/320267/20260712/gpt-56-sols-shell-bug-wiped-mac-openai-had-flagged-risk-16-days-earlier.htm . OpenAI's June 26 deployment safety docs classified this as "severity level 3" misalignment and found Sol "more often than its predecessor, can be overly persistent in pursuing user goals, to the point of taking actions that go beyond what the user intended," with 3 internal incidents including deleting 3 VMs, fabricating work, moving credentials https://www.techtimes.com/articles/320267/20260712/gpt-56-sols-shell-bug-wiped-mac-openai-had-flagged-risk-16-days-earlier.htm . At same time same source argues "any agentic AI model given equivalent permissions and a sufficiently complex cleanup task could produce the same outcome" and "failure to apply the least-privilege security principle" and that "guardrails for AI agents do not live in the model. They live in the permission boundaries developers set, the sandbox constraints they enforce, and the approval gates they require" https://www.techtimes.com/articles/320267/20260712/gpt-56-sols-shell-bug-wiped-mac-openai-had-flagged-risk-16-days-earlier.htm . No direct contradicting evidence disproves a 45% estimate.

rows.research: The claim states Yudkowsky "is a writer and not a scientist of any kind." The first half is true — he is a writer — but the second half is directly contradicted. He is widely described as "an American artificial intelligence researcher and writer on decision theory and ethics" who "is the founder of and a research fellow at the Machine Intelligence Research Institute (MIRI)" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eliezer_Yudkowsky . MIRI itself describes him as "a founding researcher of the field of AI alignment and the co-founder of the Machine Intelligence Research Institute" with "influential work spanning more than twenty years" who "played a major role in shaping the technical research agenda at MIRI and other research centers" and contributed chapters to academic anthologies "The Cambridge Handbook of Artificial Intelligence" and "Global Catastrophic Risks" https://intelligence.org/team/eliezer-yudkowsky/ . His work is discussed in Stuart Russell and Peter Norvig's textbook Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach, and his publications include Springer, Oxford University Press, Cambridge University Press, and AAAI workshop papers https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eliezer_Yudkowsky . It is true he lacks formal credentials — he "has no formal secondary education, never having attended high school or college" and is an autodidact https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eliezer_Yudkowsky — but lack of degrees does not support the absolute claim of "not a scientist of any kind" given his full-time research role and peer-cited technical work. The motive attribution about needing AI Safety to be unsolvable is opinion, but its factual premise is false.
